findings: AUTH-INV-06 (docs/authority.md:59,101 — expiry/revocation checked at EXECUTION time, not only at planning) is genuinely enforced in the main path: orchestrator/runtime/flow.py::_execute re-reads the registry record + revocation list immediately before the side effect and fails closed on absent/inactive/revoked/expired. But the re-check is parent-centric: the ExecutionEngine authority re-check evaluates the PLANNING-TIME child delegation snapshot (flow.py:625 passes `child` into ExecutionRequest at flow.py:996-1004; engine.py:303-308 uses req.delegation), and child-scope ⊆ live-parent-scope (AUTH-INV-04) is verified only at issuance (control/delegation.py:426; module comment line 17 'containment checked at creation') — it is never re-derived at execution against the freshly re-read parent.

risks: A future caller that invokes ExecutionEngine directly with a child delegation snapshot would silently rely on issuance-time containment: a parent scope narrowed between planning and execution would not be re-checked at execution

A residual TOCTOU window exists between the registry re-read (flow.py:971) and the actual side effect; expiry can lapse inside it (inherent to the design, but unmeasured here)
